title: Prefill Sleuth: runtime kernel tuner using short-horizon probes and phase-aware predictors
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Reduce 95th/99th tail latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads by automatically picking the best kernel implementation per-request using lightweight short-horizon probes and phase-aware sequence-length predictors. The tuner must be safe for production (no large latency regressions), low-overhead (<0.5% token-cost increase), and compatible with Dedicated/Private deployments.

Background: Prefill/kernel choice is a dominant factor in per-request latency variability across heterogeneous GPUs and variable sequence length distributions. Existing heuristics are static and miss micro-phase shifts (e.g., long out-of-distribution prompts, dense-token bursts). This ticket prototypes a hybrid strategy combining: (1) a tiny per-request probe (micro-batch prefill of Nprobe tokens with stripped IO) to measure kernel latency/memory watermark on current machine, (2) a phase-aware predictor that classifies requests into prefill/decode phase buckets based on token-density features and recent client history, and (3) an online bandit-style selector that uses the probe + predictor as context to choose a kernel and track regret with rollback.

Design summary:
- Probe: run a micro-prefill of 4-8 tokens with conservative memory flags; record per-kernel latency, peak memory, and KV-cache warmup behavior. Probe must be cancellable and bounded (timeout 40ms).
- Predictor: lightweight model (XGBoost logistic or small MLP) trained on host/arch/seq_len_percentiles/token_entropy to map to phase buckets: SHORT, MID, LONG, DENSE. Predictor runs in <200us.
- Selector: contextual multi-armed bandit (Thompson sampling with Gaussian priors) that uses probe signals + predictor bucket to choose kernel variant (e.g., fused-attn, tiled-attn, quant-fallback). Model updates aggregated per-host and shared via aggregated telemetry.
- Safety: an adaptive fallback policy (latency-sla guardrail) triggers immediate rollback to a conservative kernel if observed latency exceeds expected by 2x or memory watermark crosses 80% of device.
- Telemetry: emit per-request kernel_choice, probe_measurements, predicted_bucket, chosen_kernel_latency, memory_watermark, and regret. Build dashboards for token-cost delta and tail-latency histograms.

Success metrics:
- Reduce 95th tail token latency by >= 10% on mixed workloads in our benchmark suite.
- Keep average token-cost change <= +0.5%.
- Probe overhead < 0.6% of requests.

Compatibility: Configurable via model-config: "kernel_tuner": {"enabled": boolean, "probe_tokens": int, "safety_margin_ms": int}. Must be toggleable per-customer for Dedicated/Private.

Rollout plan:
1) Prototype in staging with synthetic workload (Phase 1) — metric collection and canary.
2) Canary on low-volume tenant (Phase 2) for 2 weeks with strict SLA guardrails.
3) Gradual ramp with online monitoring and automatic rollback if regressions found (Phase 3).
